prerequisites: Having completed Physics and Mathematics courses during high school.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Creativity and inventive spirit in solving scientific-technical problems.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Ability to fluently use computing at a user level.
Be able to explain in an understandable way the phenomena and processes related to the basic aspects of Physics using appropriate magnitudes and units.
Ability to solve Physics problems that reinforce theoretical knowledge and serve as an introduction to subsequent applications of interest for engineering.
Analyze physical phenomena and take experimental data for their study.

syllabus_topics: TOPIC 1: OSCILLATIONS. Simple harmonic motion. Types of oscillations.
TOPIC 2: CENTRAL FORCE FIELDS. ELECTROSTATIC FIELD. Coulomb's Law. Electrostatic field. Gauss's Theorem. Electrostatic potential and potential energy. Conductors. Capacitors.
TOPIC 3: ELECTRIC CURRENT. Direct current. Circuit analysis.
TOPIC 4: MAGNETOSTATIC FIELD. Magnetic forces. Biot-Savart Law. Ampere's Circuital Law.
TOPIC 5: ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION. Faraday-Henry Law. Induction coefficients: self-induction and mutual induction.
TOPIC 6: WAVES. Characterization of waves. Electromagnetic waves: propagation.
teaching_methods: Workshop/laboratory practices (case study method, small group lab work, report writing)
Group study and work (for lab reports and other assignments)
Tutorials (individual or small group doubt resolution and guidance)
Theoretical classes (expository method/master class, with practical examples)
Practical classes (problem solving and exercise resolution)

assessment_methods.method: Final exam (written test of theory and problem-solving, including multiple-choice and exercise resolution)
Laboratory practices (monitoring of practice execution and critical evaluation of submitted reports or proposed questions)

assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by a final written exam (85%) and laboratory practices (15%), which include monitoring of execution and evaluation of submitted reports. No specific minimum marks per component or resit arrangements are detailed in the syllabus.
